Public Healthcare Facilities in Cuttack District, Odisha
A Structured Reference Guide to District, Community, and Primary Health Facilities
Overview
Cuttack district is one of Odisha's most populous and historically significant districts, and its headquarters town, Cuttack city, has long served as a major medical hub for the wider region — it hosts the SCB Medical College and Hospital, one of the oldest and largest tertiary-care government teaching hospitals in eastern India. Below this tertiary tier, the district's public healthcare network follows the same tiered structure used across India: village-level Sub-Centres feed into Primary Health Centres (PHCs), which refer upward to Community Health Centres (CHCs), which in turn refer to the District Headquarters Hospital (DHH) as the district's secondary-level referral point. This structure is coordinated locally by the Chief District Medical Officer (CDMO), Cuttack, under the Odisha Department of Health & Family Welfare, and follows standards set nationally through the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) via the National Health Mission (NHM), most recently revised in 2022.
Facility Types
District Headquarters Hospital (DHH), Cuttack
The DHH functions as the district's main secondary-level referral hospital, distinct from the tertiary-care SCB Medical College and Hospital located in the same city. It is intended to receive cases referred from CHCs, PHCs, and Sub-Centres across Cuttack district's blocks, and to provide a broader range of inpatient, diagnostic, and specialist services than block-level facilities. The exact current designation, address, and administrative details of the DHH should be confirmed with the CDMO Cuttack office, as this document does not independently verify facility-specific particulars.
Community Health Centres (CHCs)
CHCs are block-level referral units, generally built to serve a population of roughly 80,000 to 120,000 people, with lower population norms in hilly or tribal areas. Cuttack district's blocks (such as Athagarh, Banki, Salepur, Niali, Tangi-Choudwar, and others) are each expected to have a CHC serving as the referral point for PHCs within that block. A CHC is designed to have around 30 inpatient beds, an operation theatre, basic diagnostic and blood storage facilities, and specialist coverage in areas such as medicine, surgery, obstetrics/gynaecology, and paediatrics, though actual staffing and equipment levels vary by centre. Centres equipped for round-the-clock emergency obstetric and newborn care may additionally be designated First Referral Units (FRUs).
Primary Health Centres (PHCs)
PHCs are typically the first point of contact with a qualified doctor for rural and semi-urban residents, each covering a population of around 20,000 to 30,000. A PHC supervises a cluster of Sub-Centres in its area and is expected to provide outpatient consultation, a small number of inpatient beds (around four to six), basic laboratory testing, and normal delivery services at PHCs designated for 24x7 care. PHCs also oversee ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) and ANM (Auxiliary Nurse Midwife) workers operating at the village level.
Sub-Centres and Health & Wellness Centres
The most peripheral public health facilities are Health Sub-Centres, increasingly being upgraded as Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs). These are generally staffed by an ANM and a Community Health Officer and focus on preventive and promotive care — immunization, antenatal check-ups, and basic screening — referring more complex cases upward to the PHC.
What Each Facility Handles
District Headquarters Hospital
Complex and emergency cases referred from CHCs and PHCs across the district
Broader specialist consultation and surgical services than block-level facilities
Diagnostics, blood storage/blood bank services, and larger inpatient bed capacity
Possible empanelment under schemes such as Ayushman Bharat–PM-JAY for cashless treatment (current empanelment status should be verified locally)
Acts as the secondary-level referral hospital for the district, with onward referral to SCB Medical College and Hospital or another tertiary centre for cases needing higher-level specialty or super-specialty care
Community Health Centres
Referral care for PHCs within the block, plus specialist consultation for patients approaching directly
Inpatient care (around 30 beds), minor and some major surgical procedures, and operation theatre services
Emergency obstetric care and institutional deliveries, particularly at centres designated as First Referral Units
Basic diagnostics including laboratory services and, at many centres, X-ray facilities
Primary Health Centres
Outpatient consultation for common illnesses, minor injuries, and chronic disease follow-up
Antenatal, natal, and postnatal care, including normal deliveries at 24x7 PHCs
Immunization, family planning services, and national health programme delivery (TB, malaria, non-communicable disease screening, and similar)
Basic laboratory tests (blood, urine, blood sugar, malaria rapid tests, and similar)
First-level stabilization and referral of serious cases to a CHC or the District Headquarters Hospital
How to Reach Them (General Guidance)
Since exact addresses and phone numbers are not being invented here, the following general approaches can help locate and reach the correct facility:
Ask the local ASHA worker, ANM, or Anganwadi worker — they know the nearest Sub-Centre and PHC serving a household and can help with referral upward if needed.
Every block headquarters in Cuttack district has a CHC; the block administrative (Block Development/Tahasil) office can confirm its exact location.
The Cuttack district administration's official website and the CDMO Cuttack office maintain listings of health facilities; these should be treated as the authoritative source for confirmed addresses and phone numbers.
The National Health Mission (NHM) Odisha and Odisha Directorate of Health Services websites publish facility directories and health scheme information at the state level.
The 108 (emergency response) and 102 (patient transport / maternal-child) ambulance services can be used to reach an appropriate facility in an emergency, and can also help route a patient to the correct level of care.
For the District Headquarters Hospital specifically, and to distinguish it from SCB Medical College and Hospital in the same city, confirm the current address and scope of services with the district health administration before travelling.
When to Go to District Hospital vs PHC
Go to a PHC (or Sub-Centre) first for:
Routine illnesses — fever, cold, minor infections, common ailments
Antenatal check-ups, immunizations, and family planning services
Normal, uncomplicated deliveries at a 24x7-designated PHC
Basic diagnostic tests and follow-up for chronic conditions already under management
Minor injuries and first-aid level care
Go to (or be referred to) a CHC for:
Cases needing minor surgery, specialist consultation, or inpatient observation beyond what a PHC can provide
Complicated deliveries or emergency obstetric care, especially at an FRU-designated CHC
Situations where the PHC has stabilized a patient but recommended referral
Go directly to the District Headquarters Hospital for:
Serious emergencies — major trauma, accidents, severe medical emergencies where higher-level care is clearly needed
Conditions requiring specialist care, surgery, or diagnostics not available at PHC or CHC level
Cases already referred by a PHC or CHC as needing secondary-level hospital care
Situations covered under empanelled schemes (e.g., PM-JAY) requiring hospital-level admission — confirm current scheme coverage locally
As a general rule, the public health system is designed as a step-up referral chain: Sub-Centre → PHC → CHC → District Headquarters Hospital → Medical College Hospital, with each level equipped for progressively more complex care. In Cuttack's case, the presence of SCB Medical College and Hospital in the same city as the DHH means very serious or specialized cases may ultimately be referred there, but the DHH and CHCs remain the intended first stops for most secondary-level care under the standard referral pathway. Bypassing lower tiers is appropriate mainly in genuine emergencies, where reaching the nearest capable facility quickly — often via 108 ambulance services — matters more than following the tier order.
Sources Used
National Health Mission (NHM), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India — Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) Guidelines, 2012 and 2022 revisions, for Sub-Centres, PHCs, CHCs, and District/Sub-District Hospitals (nhm.gov.in)
Odisha Department of Health & Family Welfare / Directorate of Health Services, Government of Odisha (health.odisha.gov.in / dhsodisha.nic.in) — general reference for state health administration structure
SCB Medical College and Hospital, Cuttack — general public knowledge of its role as a major government tertiary-care teaching hospital in the district
PMC/NIH — "Health systems in India," National Center for Biotechnology Information, for general description of the CHC/PHC/Sub-Centre referral structure (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov)
World Health Organization (WHO) and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) — general public health system and primary healthcare framework references
Note on this update: Web search was not available while preparing this document, so Cuttack-specific facility names, block-level CHC listings, and current facility status were not independently re-verified from live district sources at the time of writing. The structural and functional information above is grounded in national IPHS/NHM/MoHFW standards, which apply uniformly across Odisha's districts. All Cuttack-specific facility names, addresses, and current operational status should be confirmed with the CDMO Cuttack office or Odisha Directorate of Health Services before being treated as final.
⚠ IMPORTANT NOTE ON CONTACT DETAILS
This document describes facility types, functions, and general navigation guidance only. Exact phone numbers, office addresses, named officers, and facility-specific contact details are placeholders to be filled in later using official information obtained directly from the Cuttack District Health Office / CDMO Cuttack, the Odisha Directorate of Health Services, or the National Health Mission (NHM) Odisha website. No phone numbers or addresses have been invented for this document; where specifics are not confirmed, that is stated explicitly rather than guessed.
